entries.name: BeepBite
entries.summary: Self-hosted open-source restaurant POS web application with a staff POS workspace: configured menu grid and modifiers, open tabs and seat-level check splitting, table transfer, tender recording, kitchen display, and manager-approved voids and comps. The complete code base is offered under Apache-2.0 (README also states MIT OR Apache-2.0) with no hosted or paid tiers.
features: Staff POS workspace with table bar, searchable menu grid grouped by category, modifiers, courses, and a running cart
Open tabs and walk-in tickets held across a service period
Split Check by Seat: allocate items to seats, produce per-seat totals, and tender each separately
Assign or move a table from the POS header
Tenders recorded as cash, card machine, bank transfer, or voucher
Void, comp, discount, and price override with reason codes and manager PIN approval
Kitchen display with per-station routing and expo view
Menu and recipe management with modifiers, courses, and a live 86 list
Cash drawer sessions, reconciliation, and sales reporting views
deployment: Self-hosted Go API and React frontend against an operator-owned PostgreSQL database
Single release binary for Linux and macOS on amd64 and arm64
No hosted service, vendor account, or platform fee

leaf_matches.reason: Official README and user guide document a staff-operated POS workspace that satisfies the defining core: staff start a dine-in table session or walk-in ticket and add items from a searchable menu grid grouped by category, with modifiers and courses configured in Menu & Recipes; the order accumulates as an open tab; Split Check by Seat allocates every item to seats and breaks the sent check into per-seat totals each with its own Tender action, and the table clears only once every seat is paid; the header supports assigning or moving a table; Charge opens payment with cash, card machine, bank transfer, or voucher tenders; and voids, comps, discounts, and price overrides carry reason codes, with a manager PIN step when the reason is flagged for sign-off, and are audit-logged. The /q quick-POS self-order mode is explicitly documented as having no held-open tabs, no splits, and no voids/comps, so it is not used as evidence for this leaf.
